claims: The Lyrid meteor shower peaks on April 21–22, 2026.
The best viewing of the Lyrid meteor shower is after midnight until dawn.
15–20 meteors per hour are expected from the Lyrid meteor shower.
The Lyrid meteor shower has minimal moon interference.
The meteors radiate from the constellation Lyra in the northeast.
Lyrid meteors can appear anywhere in the sky.
The peak activity of the Lyrid meteor shower occurs in the early hours of April 22, 2026.
The Lyrid meteor shower is caused by debris from Comet Thatcher.
Comet Thatcher takes 415 years to orbit the sun.
